root_cause.text: The EIP-93 crypto driver’s detach/unregister routine in `drivers/crypto/inside-secure/eip93/eip93-main.c` used the wrong loop index for hash algorithms, so it repeatedly called `crypto_unregister_ahash()` on the same `eip93_algs[i]` entry instead of the current `eip93_algs[j]`, leading to double-unregister and a kernel panic.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `crypto_unregister_ahash(&eip93_algs[i]->alg.ahash);` to `crypto_unregister_ahash(&eip93_algs[j]->alg.ahash);`, and the CVE/commit message explicitly says “During driver detach, the same hash algorithm is unregistered multiple times due to a wrong iterator.”

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct is present in this function. In `eip93_unregister_algs(unsigned int i)`, the hash case uses the wrong index: `case EIP93_ALG_TYPE_HASH: crypto_unregister_ahash(&eip93_algs[i]->alg.ahash); break;`. The loop iterates with `for (j = 0; j < i; j++)`, so the correct entry should be `eip93_algs[j]`, not `eip93_algs[i]`. Because this code repeatedly unregisters the same array element when hash algorithms are encountered, it matches the root cause of double-unregister/panic. There is no fix here, since the incorrect `i` is still present and no special handling prevents the bug.
